title: Align battery footer and light surfaces
description: Match the redesign's colored battery footer and light palette, adding truthful time-left/time-to-full estimates from live energy and power data while preserving dark mode.
acceptance_criteria: Sidebar battery icon uses the redesign's green semantic color; discharging shows estimated time left; charging shows estimated time to full; invalid or unavailable telemetry omits estimates; light detail background, sidebar, card fill, and card borders match the redesign; compact/wide tests and quality gates pass.

title: Harden fan and power telemetry UI
description: Reject unusable all-zero hardware fan curves and zero-valued controller power limits, correct NVIDIA fan units and live watt summaries, remove duplicate sensor provenance, and align Fans/Advanced tuning controls with the current dashboard card-toggle pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid fan curve data renders a truthful unavailable state instead of a collapsed graph; live package/GPU draw replaces misleading 0 W limit facts; fan units and max RPM are correct; fan and overclock toggles use the dashboard pattern; precise controls match the current visual system; compact and wide tests plus full quality gates pass.

title: Add CPU clock and package power telemetry
notes: Implemented root-owned GLib/GIO RAPL sampler, versioned read-only system D-Bus API, hardened systemd service, D-Bus group policy, sysusers entry, Nix package/module, fail-soft Flutter client, live sensor propagation, and Power-page CPU clock/package power facts. Verified with 431 Flutter tests, flutter analyze, native sampler/contract tests, Impeccable detector, Linux release build, nix-build, and NixOS module evaluation.
close_reason: Package power service, NixOS packaging, Flutter integration, UI, and automated coverage completed.

title: Polish power profile ownership UI
Integrate power profiles daemon with Power controls
description: Route standard power profiles through power-profiles-daemon so amd-pstate and platform_profile remain synchronized, retain Lenovo-only Extreme and Custom modes, use the Yaru-native selector, and add truthful AC/custom staging affordances where backend support exists.
design: Use a dedicated unprivileged PPD D-Bus service. PPD owns standard profile writes; direct Legion profile writes remain only for firmware profiles PPD cannot represent. Do not expose duplicate amd-pstate writers.
acceptance_criteria: Standard Quiet/Balanced/Performance writes use PPD when available; Lenovo-only modes remain explicit; the selector is Yaru-native and responsive; power-limit staging cannot apply outside supported prerequisites; automated tests and Linux quality gates pass.
notes: Implemented shared PPD D-Bus coordination for Power and Dashboard. Standard profiles use org.freedesktop.UPower.PowerProfiles; vendor Custom/Extreme pair with PPD performance and use the Legion direct writer. Firmware choices are validated before PPD mutation, and returning from unrecognized vendor profiles repairs PPD no-ops. Power UI uses YaruChoiceChipBar, displays daemon/driver and AC state, stages limit edits behind Custom+AC, and rolls back earlier batch writes on later failure. Verified against live PPD 0.30 properties. Quality gates: 421 tests, flutter analyze, Impeccable detector, Linux release build.
close_reason: PPD integration, Yaru selector, staged guarded limits, rollback, tests, and documentation completed.

title: Deploy Kernel 7 Legion fan driver
description: Replace the active pre-Kernel-7 LenovoLegionLinux read_file_fix pin with a tested immutable revision containing upstream PRs #423 and #434, rebuild and reboot NixOS, then verify the synthetic legion platform device and legion_hwmon on Lenovo 82Y4 / M1CN48WW. Preserve existing dirty NixOS configuration changes. Exact evidence and safe procedure are in docs/architecture/fan-controller-kernel-7-handoff.md.
acceptance_criteria: NixOS source pin contains upstream merges 1570dba2c8c3079115439f43e50d2891813c38d9 and c52b4f293c4e8c00acf6bfba2bbd06b862cdf4a1; rebuilt generation boots; PNP0C09 remains owned by acpi-ec; synthetic platform:legion/legion binds; kernel logs show successful probe; legion_hwmon exposes truthful fan limits and curve points; frontend reads the real curve; results are recorded without unsafe live EC rebinding.
notes:
Live probe after the Power-page report: kernel is 7.2.0, but the booted legion-laptop.ko still exports acpi*:PNP0C09:* and /sys/bus/platform/drivers/legion has no bound legion or PNP device. PNP0C09:00 remains present under the ACPI EC path. Consequently no cpu_*_powerlimit or gpu_*_powerlimit sysfs files exist, so the frontend truthfully has no limits to render. Build and boot the upstream-pinned NixOS generation, then run the documented read-only verification.
Live Kernel 7 follow-up: legion_hwmon is now bound and exposes fan RPM/max and 10 curve points, but all thermal thresholds/hysteresis/ramp values and all GPU PWM values are zero. The frontend must reject this unusable curve; driver/firmware validation remains incomplete.

title: Complete handoff navigation migration
description: Match the handoff top-level navigation only after omitted functionality is migrated. Target: Dashboard, Power, Fans, Battery, Lighting, dGPU, Automation, Settings. Remove route dispatch and AppSection values for Devices, Display, and Diagnostics only after every control has a designed home.
acceptance_criteria: No current control is lost; Devices, Display, and Diagnostics functionality is migrated or covered by an explicit design decision; target navigation and compact/wide index mapping work; persisted navigation and tests are updated safely.

title: Apply Yaru handoff to Fans page
description: Implement Phase 4 of the Yaru handoff plan. Treat the generated design as the visual source of truth while preserving fan safety and existing serialization. Redesign the action row, preset dialog, curve editor, telemetry, and safety copy with the shared metric and responsive-card primitives.
acceptance_criteria: Preset and max-fan actions are prominent; CPU/GPU temperatures and fan RPM are telemetry-forward; the curve editor remains keyboard/mouse usable without overflow; safety copy remains clear; light/dark and compact/wide layouts pass; tests and analyzer pass.
notes:
Post-close repair: restored the handoff's curve-first composition with direct context-aware presets, useful unavailable-controller state, live CPU/GPU telemetry, Custom accent, bounded curve edits, and responsive compact/wide layouts. Fixed controller hwmon symlink discovery and separate global hwmon RPM fallback. Focused Fans tests, full suite, analyzer, detector, and release build pass.
Visual cleanup follow-up: removed the legacy Fan curve/profile/refresh page header, replaced CPU/GPU chips with the official Yaru-themed segmented ToggleButtons presentation, replaced the unavailable chart overlay with a compact information state, and replaced Controller safeguards/admin badge with capability-gated native Fan controls. Full tests and analyzer pass.
Post-close state-truth follow-up: recommendations no longer auto-select, preset chips use semantic accents, Custom violet is limited to dirty custom curves, and Yaru component colours are applied directly rather than via a nested primary override. Kernel 7 synthetic platform-root discovery and regression tests were added; backend deployment is tracked by lllf-cqn.8.

title: Finish Lighting hardware validation and model cleanup
description: Resume Claude session 29b963b8-3021-43d8-97a4-821d550dc699 at the exact checkpoint recorded in the handoff plan. Commit 568bc5b applied a measured 0.88 green gain. Full white is neutral at full brightness and purple-shifted when dim. tool/_step.dart step 5 (per-key rainbow) was sent, but no hardware result was recorded. After validation, generalize the OpenRgbDevice model name now that native Spectrum is the primary path and decide whether the diagnostic tool should be retained.
acceptance_criteria: Step 5 result is recorded; native static painting and representative effects are verified on hardware; low-brightness behavior is either measured and fixed or documented; OpenRGB-specific naming no longer describes shared native device state; tests and analyzer pass.
notes: Post-close regression repair: OpenRGB process/probe failures no longer hide a usable native Spectrum keyboard, while genuine OpenRGB errors remain visible when native Spectrum is unavailable. Added service, bloc, and degraded-page regression coverage; Lighting suite, analyzer, and release build pass.
close_reason: Lighting hardware validation, adaptive dim calibration, Direct streaming protocol, model cleanup, tests, and analyzer all complete.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Hardware validation 2026-08-29: tool/_step.dart step 5 sent=true for 111 LEDs at brightness 9. User observed the expected static per-key rainbow.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Step 6 sent=true for 111 LEDs at brightness 9. Section mapping is correct. Dim-white remaining keys have a slight purple tint, which the user considers acceptable.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Dim-white calibration: coarse bands bracketed neutral gain between 0.92 and 0.96; refined 0.93 and 0.95 bands looked equivalent. Selected midpoint 0.94. Step 11 sent all 111 LEDs at brightness 3 with gain 0.94; user rated it acceptable. Production implementation interpolates from 0.94 at device levels 0-3 to the measured 0.88 at level 9 and repaints the cached frame after brightness changes.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Final hardware gate: step 8 confirmed only Escape illuminated red. Initial animation was static because the active profile had never been configured for Aura Sync/Direct. Added the authoritative OpenRGB Gen 7/8 sequence: CA set/get active-profile transaction, one-time D0 Direct enable, then CB profile configuration for effect 0x0D before repeated A1 frames. Step 12 streamed 900 frames over 30 seconds at 30 FPS; user confirmed smooth continuous animation without flicker or dropped keys. Shared OpenRgbDevice was renamed RgbLightingDevice; diagnostic retained.

title: Validate telemetry service on installed NixOS

title: Define authoritative power-limit defaults
description: The Power page now stages and reverts edits to the live controller baseline, but Restore defaults cannot be implemented truthfully because the Legion backend exposes writable current limits without a complete authoritative default set. Determine whether firmware, a model database, or an upstream CLI command can provide per-model defaults, then expose Restore defaults only when that source is available.
design: Do not infer defaults from slider bounds or label CPUDefaultPowerLimit as a complete preset. Reuse the staged batch and rollback path once trustworthy values exist.
acceptance_criteria: A documented authoritative source supplies defaults for every exposed limit; unsupported models do not show a restore action; restoring is AC/Custom gated, confirmed, rollback-safe, and tested.

acceptance_criteria: Automation rules represent existing triggers/actions and retain run-now/poll status appropriately; Settings contains Appearance, Backend, About, diagnostics, and retained Boot Logo functionality; Win Key, Camera, Overdrive, and Refresh Rate have explicit homes or tracked design decisions; tests and analyzer pass.

title: Apply Yaru handoff to Battery and dGPU pages

acceptance_criteria: Common mode switching matches the handoff and uses the mode accent; advanced limits are discoverable without visual noise; custom/overclock warnings remain adjacent to controls; responsive light/dark layouts pass; tests and analyzer pass.
notes:
Paused before the Power redesign while lllf-cqn.8 deploys and validates the Kernel 7 Legion backend. The frontend now supports both legacy and synthetic Legion platform roots.

Second post-close UI refinement: mode controls now hug their label content with no fixed width; Wrap only moves controls when horizontal space is exhausted. Added regression coverage proving short and long labels receive different widths.
close_reason: Completed Phase 5 Power handoff and all quality gates.
